Kimi write jobs now run without `--auto`, and the change is committed as `9e9f2b4`.

- Read-only jobs still use `--plan`.
- Write jobs, including resumed ones, now pass no mode flag and keep `-p` with the prompt.
- Only `subtask/worker.py` changed.
- One test fails, `test_fast_server_publishes_what_fastmcp_would`. It fails the same way before my change, so this fix did not cause it.
- I did not run a real Kimi CLI. Without `--auto`, I'm assuming `-p` runs without approval prompts.
- You are on a detached checkout (no branch name). The commit sits on top of `3f731f6` there. Tell me if you want it put on a named branch.

It checks the process's command line. A reused pid will not have the right text in it.

- It reads `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` (`subtask/jobs.py:98`).
- It returns true only if that text has `subtask.worker` and the job id (line 103). The code comment on that line says this guards against pid reuse.
- Before that, `os.waitpid(pid, WNOHANG)` (line 93) catches our own child that already exited. It reaps it, and `_alive` returns false.
- If the pid is not our child, it skips that step and goes on to the command line check.
- If `/proc/<pid>` is missing, it returns false.
- Other read errors, like no `/proc` at all, return true.
- If `job_id` is empty, only `subtask.worker` is checked. That is a weaker test.
